text:
alex: Kicked off a delta-run today comparing our current warmup (prefix cache only) vs a small KV-priming heuristic + kernel hinting. Wanted to share quick findings and get thoughts.

mike-bench-bot: started job 1842007777-delta-shadow (shadow-run, model=gptx-13b, batchshape=auto, replay=shadow)

sophia: nice! what's the traffic mix and token distribution you fed? :thinking_face:

alex: short summary: 60s shadow window sampled from production (90/10 chat/complete), median prompt length ~25 tokens, target gen length 64. We also ran a synthetic steady replay for 5m for repeatability.

kevin: initial numbers (single A100 pool, default kernels):\n- warm (prefix-only): P50=48ms, P95=380ms, P99=980ms\n- cold (no priming): P50=62ms, P95=1.9s, P99=4.7s
Observations: big P95/P99 regression during scale-up spikes.

tara: did you hit burst credits? and which kernel path triggered during the spike? could be kernel fallback slower path.

alex: yes: burst credits depleted after ~22s of sustained QPS in the synthetic run. We saw fallback from int8-packed kernels to fp16-fallback for some layers at scale-up step 2. Stack trace snippet from runtime profiler:\n```
[2024-11-03 14:22:12] kernel_selector: selected packed_int8 for attention_layer_1
[2024-11-03 14:22:34] kernel_exec: fallback -> fp16_attention_slow (reason: memory_fragmentation)
[2024-11-03 14:22:35] kv_cache: priming_hits=0 priming_misses=237
```

sophia: interesting — memory_fragmentation threshold should not cause full kernel fallback unless KV allocation spikes. Did you try a small KV prefill to reduce misses?

alex: ran one micro-experiment with KV-priming size=8 prefixes per session. Results: P95 dropped from 1.9s -> 520ms during the same surge, P99 from 4.7s -> 1.2s. Burst credit usage improved (spent ~40% less).

kevin: looks promising. What's the command you used to reproduce? so we can add to the harness. :memo:

alex: command: \n```
./harness/run_delta.sh --model gptx-13b --shadow-sample 60 --kv-prime 8 --kernel-hint packed_int8 --replay synthetic5m --record-artifacts
```

tara: two quick asks before we escalate: 1) confirm this generalizes to larger sequence lengths (128/256) 2) try the dedicated pool test (reserve GPUs) because burst credits behave differently there.

mike-bench-bot: job 1842007777-delta-shadow completed: artifacts -> s3://redwood-qa/bench/1842007777/ (profiles, flamegraphs, raw-traces)

kevin: pulled the flamegraphs — the tail is dominated by kernel exec stalls when fallback happens, and a secondary hotspot is kv cache allocation during first writes. I'll open a short profiling PR to annotate the kernel selector logs.

sophia: agree on dedicated pool test. If KV priming reduces cold P95 by ~60% we should consider moving priming heuristic to runtime as an opt-in flag for Dedicated customers.

alex: next steps I propose: 1) run 128/256 seq long synthetic sweep, 2) dedicated-pool delta run, 3) add a lightweight prefetch + kernel-hint experiment in canary. I'll post results in a follow-up thread. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

tara: +1, please add a note about the cost delta in the report (token-level accounting). some customers care if priming increases upfront GPU work.

alex: noted — initial estimate is ~3-5% extra GPU cycles for priming but 30-50% less tail latency / fewer retries. I'll include cost vs tail-latency tradeoff.

sophia: thanks — this is a useful regression-mitigation pattern. also add the exact runtime flags so eng-sre can simulate the burst-credit timeline.

kevin: ACK, I'll open a tiny script to convert the bench traces into burst-credit vs latency timelines and share it.

alex: thanks all. wrapping up here, follow-up with artifacts link and the 128/256 sweep plan tomorrow. :rocket:
